rationale: Chief Justice Roberts, as the assigning justice in the majority, is most likely to write the opinion himself given his minimalist instincts and desire to control the narrowest possible holding — likely denying certiorari or resolving on statutory grounds while avoiding the broad constitutional question. Thomas and Gorsuch are likely to write separately to press their originalist view that foreign states are categorically not Fifth Amendment persons, while the four dissenters are likely to produce one or more dissents emphasizing the circuit split and the need for constitutional resolution.
